meta.title: Al-Midan Ya Hamidan | Skill proves itself
meta.description: A Saudi platform that assesses and develops talent through job-specific work simulations, clear evidence and explainable evaluation.

home.heroLead: A Saudi platform where organizations define what a job requires, candidates demonstrate their ability in realistic work simulations, and Midan evaluates real performance with structured evidence. The final decision stays with a human reviewer.
home.explorerEyebrow: From job description to the field
home.explorerTitle: Pick a field and watch a line from a job description become work you can prove
home.explorerNote: An illustrative example of the idea, not a live assessment or a real job.
home.levelsTitle: What does “{skill}” look like at each level?
home.levelsHint: Choose a level to read the behavior behind it
home.candidateTitle: For those who want their work to be seen
home.candidateBody: One account to apply to many organizations. Learn your strengths from your work rather than from claims about it, and what to develop next.
home.organizationTitle: For those who want to see before deciding
home.organizationBody: Build assessments from job responsibilities and review evidence against shared criteria, under your own brand, with data isolated from other organizations.
trust: MIDAN never makes a final hiring decision
It never rejects a candidate on a score alone
It never invents evidence or qualifications
It never publishes an assessment without human approval
home.closingQuote: Instead of asking candidates what they know, we let them prove how they work.

tech.label: Technology
tech.jobLine: Monitor cybersecurity alerts and respond to incidents.
tech.task: You have one hour of system logs and two alerts. Decide which is a real incident, what happens next, and why.
tech.deliverable: A short incident report backed by log lines
levels: No valid evidence in the submission.
Reads logs and spots obvious errors with guidance.
Connects events but misses some patterns.
Identifies the likely cause and supports it with the right lines.
Rules out alternatives and proposes monitoring to prevent a repeat.

finance.label: Finance
finance.jobLine: Prepare monthly reports and analyze budget variances.
finance.task: Here are a store branch's quarterly figures. Explain the three largest variances and what you recommend to management.
finance.deliverable: A one-page memo and a variance table
levels: No valid evidence in the submission.
Calculates variances without explaining them.
Explains the major variances in general terms.
Separates price and volume effects and ties them to an operational cause.
Estimates the coming impact and proposes a measurable action.

legal.label: Legal
legal.jobLine: Review commercial contracts and identify risks.
legal.task: Review a four-page supply contract. Pull out the main risks and propose alternative wording for two clauses.
legal.deliverable: A ranked risk list and proposed wording
levels: No valid evidence in the submission.
Summarizes clauses without assessing them.
Spots clear risks but misses how they combine.
Ranks risks by impact and cites the right clause.
Balances protection with business interest and proposes negotiable wording.

engineering.label: Engineering
engineering.jobLine: Follow project execution and review drawings on site.
engineering.task: A conflict between a drawing and a site report is delaying a whole phase. Identify the conflict and sequence a resolution plan.
engineering.deliverable: A request for information and a timed resolution plan
levels: No valid evidence in the submission.
Recognizes the basic elements of a drawing.
Notices the visible conflict without estimating its impact.
Pinpoints the conflict and its effect on the schedule.
Anticipates later conflicts and proposes a fix that reduces rework.

events.label: Events
events.jobLine: Run daily event operations and staff teams.
events.task: Two hours before opening, a key supplier is missing and the entry route has changed. Reassign the team and decide what comes first.
events.deliverable: An updated operating plan and a message to the team
levels: No valid evidence in the submission.
Lists problems without ordering them.
Sets priorities but offers no alternatives.
Decides clearly and shows the effect on visitors and staff.
Builds a fallback plan and decision points for what may come next.

healthcare.label: Healthcare
healthcare.jobLine: Coordinate patient care and improve the patient journey.
healthcare.task: An outpatient clinic gets repeated complaints about waiting times. Analyze a week of data and propose an improvement that doesn't affect patient safety.
healthcare.deliverable: A brief analysis and an improvement proposal
levels: No valid evidence in the submission.
Reads and summarizes the numbers.
Identifies peak times without explaining them.
Links waiting to a specific cause and backs it with data.
Balances efficiency with safety and sets a metric to track improvement.

flow.title: Organizations define. Candidates demonstrate. Midan evaluates with evidence.

how.title: One journey, from the job to the evidence
how.lead: Midan builds the assessment from the work itself, preserves the exact version each candidate was assessed on, and keeps the decision with people.

steps.title: Define the job
steps.body: The organization sets responsibilities and required skills, and maps them to a central skills taxonomy.

steps.title: Build the assessment
steps.body: MIDAN proposes tasks and rubrics from the job. The team reviews and edits everything.

steps.title: Approve and publish
steps.body: Nothing is published without human approval, and every published version is immutable.

steps.title: Take the assessment
steps.body: The candidate completes tasks and uploads evidence in an experience carrying the organization's brand.

steps.title: Evaluate
steps.body: Objective questions are graded automatically, MIDAN proposes evidence-backed scores, and uncertain cases go to a human reviewer.

steps.title: Report and develop
steps.body: The organization sees every criterion. Candidates see what the organization releases, with steps to develop.

how.scaleLead: No numbers without meaning. Every level describes what was actually seen in the candidate's work.

scale.name: No valid evidence
scale.body: The submission isn't enough to judge the skill.

scale.name: Basic
scale.body: Applies the fundamentals in simple situations, with guidance.

scale.name: Developing
scale.body: Completes most of what's needed, lacking some depth or reasoning.

scale.name: Proficient
scale.body: Works independently and supports decisions with evidence.

scale.name: Advanced
scale.body: Handles complexity, anticipates consequences and raises the quality of the solution.

candidates.title: Let your work speak
candidates.lead: Whether you're a student, a fresh graduate or experienced, Midan gives you a way to prove your ability and see what to develop next.

points.title: One account for every organization
points.body: One professional profile to apply to many organizations. Your data isn't shared between them without your consent.

points.title: Tasks that resemble real work
points.body: Clear instructions, progress tracking and file uploads, with no questions disconnected from the job.

points.title: Results you can understand
points.body: When an organization releases results, you see what was evaluated and what supports it, not an unexplained number.

points.title: A next step for development
points.body: Recommendations linked to the skills shown in your work, to build into a practical plan.

candidates.humaidanTitle: Humaidan is with you in the Midan
candidates.humaidanBody: Midan's face and your guide here. He welcomes you to your account, and you'll see him in your assessments in the professional outfit that suits the role.

organizations.title: See the work before you decide
organizations.lead: Turn job responsibilities into a practical assessment under your brand, and review candidates with evidence and shared criteria.

points.title: Assessments from the heart of the job
points.body: MIDAN prepares the drafts. Your team edits and approves them.

points.title: Shared, recorded criteria
points.body: Every candidate is assessed on a fixed version of the assessment and rubric, and the record is preserved.

points.title: Human review where it matters
points.body: Uncertain cases go to a reviewer, and every score shows its source and evidence.

points.title: Your brand and your data
points.body: An experience with your logo and colors, data isolated from other organizations, and role-based permissions.

not: Not a conventional applicant tracking system
Not a black box that decides who gets hired

about.title: Why “Al-Midan Ya Hamidan”?
about.lead: The name comes from a saying Saudis know well: talk is one thing, the field is another. That is the idea: prove your ability where the work shows.

sections.title: The idea
sections.body: A platform that assesses people by what they can do, and helps them understand and develop their skills.

sections.title: One platform
sections.body: One central platform serving candidates and organizations, with each organization's data isolated from the others.

sections.title: The principles
sections.body: Evidence before impressions, explanation before scores, consent before sharing, and people before decisions.

sections.title: Humaidan
sections.body: Midan's face and guide. One character in different professional outfits, because the field isn't for one profession.

about.statusBody: Midan is under development. Accounts, opportunities, assessments and reports work now in a demo environment with fictional data, and public registration hasn't opened yet.

items.a: No. You can browse and apply to opportunities, but Midan's core is practical simulation and evidence-based assessment.

items.q: Does MIDAN decide who gets hired?
items.a: No. MIDAN proposes scores and cites evidence. The final decision always belongs to people at the organization.

items.q: Can organizations see all my data?
items.a: No. Each organization sees only what relates to your application with them. Sharing beyond that needs your explicit consent.

items.q: Do I need an account for each organization?
items.a: No. One Midan account lets you apply to many organizations.
That depends on the organization's settings. When released, you see skills, strengths, areas to improve and what supports them.

items.q: Will Humaidan complete the assessment for me?
items.a: No. Humaidan is Midan's character, and the work in an assessment is yours.
Not to the public yet. Midan currently runs in a demo environment with fictional data, and public registration hasn't opened.

footer.tagline: Skill proves itself. A Saudi product for assessing and developing talent through real work.
footer.status: Under development. Examples on this site are illustrative.

feedback.skills_without_evidence: Listed, but not shown anywhere in your experience or projects: {values}

suggestion.skills_without_evidence: Where it's true, describe a task in your experience or projects that used each skill.
suggestion.no_measurable_results: Where you can, state a result: a figure, a time saved, a scale handled.
suggestion.no_languages: Add a languages section, with your level in each.

development.title: Career development
development.lead: Always available to you, whatever happens with any application. Choose a role to see what it asks for.
development.evidenceNote: From results organizations released after human review.
development.gapsNote: No evidence doesn't mean weakness: it only means nothing shows it yet.

reason.no_evidence: Why it's here: this role asks for it, and nothing in your profile or assessments shows it yet.
reason.self_reported: Why it's here: you listed it, and no practical assessment has shown it yet.

development.noCatalog: There's no verified catalog of courses and certifications yet, so no links are shown. We won't suggest a course without a checked source.
development.source: Source: the sector skills databases issued by the sectoral skills councils.
development.planNote: Progress here is what you report. It doesn't verify a certificate or a skill.
development.jobTitleHint: In your own words, for example "Data analyst". It's kept as you wrote it. You can also link it to a job family from the sector workbooks below.
development.titleEntered: as you wrote it, not an official title
development.titleSkillsTitle: What published jobs with this title ask for
development.titleSkillsNone: No published job on MIDAN has a similar title yet, so there's nothing to compare. Link a job family below to see its skills.
development.titleSkillsNote: Required skills in {jobs, plural, one {# published job} other {# published jobs}} with a similar title. They're each organization's own requirements.
development.inJobs: in {count, plural, one {# job} other {# jobs}}
development.resourceReason: Why it's here: it develops {skill}, which this role asks for. A verified source, not an endorsement.
development.practiceNote: Ways to practise the skills your target role asks for. A simulated task is practice and a portfolio project is your own work: neither is employment, and neither counts as work experience. MIDAN checks only the shape of what you submit.
development.practiceEmpty: You haven't started a practice task yet. Start one from a skill above.

practiceKind.portfolio_project: Portfolio project · your own work, not employment

development.practiceSubmissionHint: Separate each part with a blank line.
development.checklistNote: It checks the shape of your submission only. It isn't an assessment, and no organization has seen it.

checklist.each_deliverable: A part for each thing to include

settings.manageData: Manage my data in my profile

hiring.outcomeNote: The decision is yours. The candidate reads what you write here as it is.
hiring.hireNeedsShortlist: To hire through a decision here, shortlist the candidate first.
hiring.messageAr: Message to the candidate in Arabic
hiring.messageEn: Message to the candidate in English
hiring.interviewersNote: You take part as the person scheduling. Only participants can join the video room and give feedback.

employers.title: Employer directory
employers.lead: The official employer registry: Saudi entities with their official names, aliases and sources. Being listed doesn't mean a partnership with Midan or jobs published here.
employers.noneBody: Try the official name, a common name or the company ID.
employers.identityNote: This is an identity record from the official registry. It doesn't mean a partnership, an account on Midan or open jobs.
employers.statedInEnglish: Entity type, sector and notes are shown as the source states them.
employers.namesLead: Aliases are other names people use. They are kept apart from the official name, with the status the source gives them.
employers.brandUsable: The source establishes permission to use this employer's brand.
employers.brandNeutral: Shown in Midan's neutral identity: the source doesn't establish permission to use this employer's logo, colors or fonts.
employers.noJobs: No opportunities connected to this employer on Midan right now. That doesn't mean the employer has no vacancies.

overview.integrationsLead: Configured means credentials are present on this server. It doesn't mean a real call has been verified.
overview.title: What needs attention
overview.lead: The platform's queues, what it holds, and whether its services are set up. Organizations manage their own workspaces; this console is for the platform team.
overview.attentionLead: Queues that need a decision or a fix, largest first. Each opens where it is dealt with.
overview.attentionTotal: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing waiting} one {# item waiting} other {# items waiting}}
overview.allClear: Nothing is waiting. Every queue is clear.

queueNote.openReview: Imported records to approve, edit or reject before anyone sees them.
queueNote.listingsPending: External listings to check before they are shown.
queueNote.uncertainMatches: Listings whose employer wasn't matched with confidence: confirm or correct the match.
queueNote.failedJobs: Background tasks that stopped: read the reason, then retry or dismiss.
queueNote.failedImports: Files that didn't import: read the reason and upload again.
queueNote.organizationsPending: New organizations that can't recruit until a person checks their registration and decides.

overview.glanceLead: Counts of what is stored right now. No trends are shown, because these are counts at this moment, not a history.

serviceNote.ai: Reads CVs and proposes scores. People make every decision.
serviceNote.daily: Private interview rooms, joined only by participants.
serviceNote.calendar: Interview events; whether attendees get emails is set on the server.
serviceNote.email: No email provider is set up. Sign-up and recovery emails use the auth service.
serviceNote.worker: Runs imports and other long tasks in the background.

imports.title: Import runs
imports.lead: Every import of the official data, with its source files, every sheet and how it was handled, and each row's status. Imports run from the command line with scripts/import-data.mjs; the workbooks stay out of the repository.

issues.priority_skill_not_in_skill_list: Priority skill missing from the skill list
issues.priority_flag_not_on_priority_list: Flagged priority, not on the priority list

issueHelp.near_duplicate_name: Two skills in the same sector whose names differ only in hamza, ta marbuta, diacritics or the article. They stay separate. Accept if they are different skills; dismiss if this is only noise.
issueHelp.matrix_only_skill: A skill that appears in a sub-sector sheet but not in the workbook's skill list, often a spelling variant. It is kept as written.
issueHelp.priority_skill_not_in_skill_list: Listed on the priority sheet but missing from the skill list. Kept as its own record, from the priority list.
issueHelp.description_without_listing: A description whose skill isn't listed anywhere else. Kept as its own record.
issueHelp.uncertain_employer_match: Confirm or change the employer on the listings screen.

imports.emptySourceNote: This source had no rows. That means none were supplied, not that no jobs exist.

review.lead: Items an import couldn't settle by itself. Nothing here was merged or discarded; deciding records your judgment and who made it.

employers.lead: The official employer registry, as imported. An entry is an identity record: it isn't a partnership, an account or a source of vacancies. Identity fields and partnership status change only through a new import of the source workbook.

listings.lead: Jobs collected from authorized sources, as collected. Each is matched to the employer registry with a stated confidence and classified against the skills reference. None is published until reviewed.
listings.emptyBody: Listings arrive through imports from authorized sources. None have been supplied yet.
listings.unclassified: Not classified: fewer than two reference skills mentioned

rules.alias_needs_review: Alias the source marks for review

reference.title: Skills reference
reference.lead: The sector skills workbooks as imported. Priority is shown two ways because the workbooks state it twice: a flag in the skill list, and a separate priority list.
reference.note: The workbooks hold no proficiency levels or skill identifiers, so none are shown or invented. Names are in Arabic only.

learning.title: Learning catalog
learning.lead: Courses and certifications shown to candidates next to a skill. Each entry needs a link a person opened and checked, and the date they checked it. The sector workbooks are not course catalogs, so nothing here comes from them.
learning.emptyBody: Candidates see skill goals and practical projects until checked entries are added.
learning.rule: Open the provider's page, check the title and that it's current, then add it with today's date. Don't add prices or durations.
learning.noneChosen: Search for a skill and choose one.

accounts.adminsLead: Administrators manage reference data, imports, listings and the catalog. They can't see CVs, assessment answers or scores.
accounts.name: Name
accounts.linkLead: Link a real organization account to the registry entity it is, after checking. This never makes it a partner.

queue.title: Background jobs
queue.lead: Long-running work such as CV analysis. Jobs retry by themselves with a growing delay; a job that runs out of attempts stays here for a person.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.lead: Changes to applications, organizations, assessments, results, interviews, decisions and administration, with who made them.

upload.title: Upload job records (CSV or JSON)
upload.lead: Only records you have permission to use. You'll see what would happen before anything is saved, nothing is published, and each record waits for review.
upload.authorizationHint: For example, the agreement or the person who gave permission. It's kept with the import.
upload.fileHint: Needs a job title and an https link for each record. Also read: employer, description, requirements, job ID, location, employment type, date. Up to 5 MB and 5,000 records.
upload.saveNote: Saving imports the valid records from this same file. Rows with problems stay in the import's record, and repeated rows are skipped.
upload.saved: Saved. Each record now waits for review below.

problem.url_not_https: The link must start with https://
problem.unknown_employment_type: Employment type not recognized: it won't be copied to a job

claims.lead: Organizations asking to manage an employer's profile and jobs. Check the evidence yourself: nothing is granted until you approve, and approval never makes the employer a partner.
claims.heading: {org} asks to manage {employer}
claims.testOrg: This is a test organization, so it can't be linked to a real employer.
claims.noteHint: A rejection needs a reason, which the organization sees.

organizations.title: Organizations
organizations.lead: Every organization recruits only after a person here approves it. Check the commercial registration against the official record before approving. Refusals and suspensions need a reason, which the audit log keeps.
organizations.documentsLead: Links last five minutes and are made for you only.
organizations.noteHint: Required to request changes or to refuse. The organization sees it.
organizations.reasonHint: Required. Kept in the audit log; the organization is notified.

nothingToDecide.draft: Not submitted yet: nothing to decide.
nothingToDecide.changes_requested: Waiting for the organization to make the requested changes.
nothingToDecide.rejected: Refused. The organization may submit a new application.

jobAnalysis.title: Skills from the sector workbooks
jobAnalysis.lead: Find which skills from the official sector skills workbooks this job's own text and requirements name. Nothing changes until you accept. Accepted skills shape the match candidates see and the assessment draft.
jobAnalysis.noneLinked: No workbook skills are linked to this job yet.
jobAnalysis.noSector: not determined: the text names fewer than two workbook skills
jobAnalysis.noProposals: No workbook skill is named in this job's text. Add a description or requirements, then analyze again.
jobAnalysis.fromFamily: A priority skill of the job family {family}, not named in the job
jobAnalysis.setSector: Also set the job's sector to {sector}
jobAnalysis.leadAll: The skills this job needs, decided by you. Suggestions read the job's own title, description and requirements; nothing changes until you accept. You can also search the official sector skills workbooks and add your own skills. Each skill is required or preferred, with the level you expect. The accepted list shapes the match candidates see and the assessment draft.
jobAnalysis.aiResult: Suggested by the AI model from the workbook skills closest to this job
jobAnalysis.similarResult: Workbook skills closest in meaning to this job
jobAnalysis.similarNote: The AI model wasn't available, so these are the workbook skills closest in meaning to the job, not the model's choice. Nothing is pre-selected: choose the ones the job really needs.
jobAnalysis.similar: Close in meaning to the job ({score})
jobAnalysis.levelsNote: Levels use MIDAN's scale: L1 Basic, L2 Developing, L3 Proficient, L4 Advanced. Leave a level unset when the job doesn't call for one.
jobAnalysis.searchTitle: Find a skill in the sector workbooks
jobAnalysis.searchPlaceholder: Type part of a skill name, in Arabic
jobAnalysis.searchNone: No workbook skill has that name.
jobAnalysis.customLead: For a skill the workbooks don't have. It stays on this job only and doesn't become a shared skill.
jobAnalysis.description: What it means for this job (optional)

team.title: Team
team.lead: Who works in this organization, and what they can do. Owners and admins manage the team, recruiters manage jobs and applicants, and reviewers evaluate work.
team.inviteNote: They accept it after signing in with this same email, from their invitations page. Emails aren't being sent yet, so let them know yourself.

invitations.title: Team invitations
invitations.lead: Organizations that invited this account to join their team.
invitations.emptyBody: When an organization invites this email, you'll find it here.

employerClaim.title: Official employer profile
employerClaim.lead: To manage an employer's profile and jobs on Midan, show that this organization represents it. A Midan administrator checks your evidence, and nothing is granted automatically.
employerClaim.notPartnership: This confirms who manages the account. It doesn't make the employer a partner of Midan.
employerClaim.pendingTitle: Your request to manage {employer} is being checked
employerClaim.pendingBody: You'll get a notification when it's decided.
employerClaim.noteHint: For example, who can confirm it, or an official letter you're attaching.
employerClaim.fileHint: A PDF, PNG or JPEG file, up to 5 MB. Only your organization's owners and admins and Midan's administrators can open it.
employerClaim.rejected: Your request to manage {employer} wasn't approved. You can send a new one.

assessmentIntel.companyTypeNote: MIDAN uses it, with the job's sector and level, to shape the fictional company in the assessments it prepares. Your organization's name is never sent.
assessmentIntel.qualityGated: MIDAN prepared this version to the MIDAN Assessment Standard, so approving it needs a ready report on its current content.
assessmentIntel.qualityNotGated: For information. Only versions MIDAN prepares must pass this check before approval.
assessmentIntel.qualityStale: Out of date: the draft changed after this report
assessmentIntel.notStandardized: This draft isn't a full MIDAN Assessment Standard package.
assessmentIntel.qualityEnglish: The checks' messages are in English.
assessmentIntel.guideAssessorOnly: For assessors only. Candidates never see this.

orgShell.overviewLead: Your jobs, your applicants, and where each person stands, in one place.
orgShell.pipelineLead: Every application, counted at its current stage.

journey.eyebrow: Welcome to the world of MIDAN
journey.lead: Where talent meets opportunity. A journey that begins with your skills and moves you closer to what's next.
journey.srTitle: The MIDAN journey, in five scenes
journey.finalTitle: Every step brings you closer to what's next.
journey.finalLead: Whether you're looking for your next role or building your team, the journey starts with one step.

stages.title: Discover opportunities
stages.body: Browse roles from organizations on MIDAN, with clear requirements, the skills each role needs, and how your profile matches.

stages.title: Show your skills
stages.body: Prove what you can do through a practical task tied to the job: clear requirements, a set deadline, and your work submitted in one place.

stages.title: Meet your future
stages.body: Once an organization shortlists you, your interview is scheduled, you confirm the time, and you join from MIDAN.

stages.title: Your next chapter
stages.body: Every step brings you closer to what's next.

checklist: Read the brief and the materials

Write a short report backed by log lines

myApplications.title: Where each application stands
myApplications.lead: Every application you've made, its current stage, and the one thing to do next.
myApplications.emptyBody: When you apply to an opportunity, it appears here with its stage and your next step.

groupLead.todo: Start or continue before the deadline. Your work saves as you go.
groupLead.waiting: A person at the organization reviews your work. You'll be notified when results are released.
groupLead.results: The organization has released these results to you.

how: You receive a practical task linked to the job you applied for.
Read the brief, then work on it and upload your files. It saves as you go.
Submit before the deadline. You'll get a receipt.
A person reviews your work. Results appear here when released.

myInterviews.title: Your interviews
myInterviews.lead: Upcoming interviews first, with their time and status. Open one to confirm or join.
myInterviews.emptyBody: When an organization shortlists you and schedules an interview, it appears here to confirm.

levels.label: Skill levels
levels.startingBody: L0 means the work doesn't yet show enough to judge the skill. It's not a failure: it's where evidence begins.

command.welcomeLead: Five steps get you from a new organization to your first published job. Start with any of them.
command.noDataYet: Your dashboard fills in as candidates apply. Nothing here is estimated.

profile.title: Complete your organization profile
profile.body: Your colors and welcome message appear in candidates' assessments.

logo.title: Add your logo

team.title: Invite your team
team.body: Recruiters and reviewers can work with you, each with their own role.

job.title: Create your first job

publish.title: Publish it
publish.body: Candidates can apply once a job is published.

command.pipelineLead: Where every applicant is now. Select a stage to see who's in it.
command.trendLead: The last eight weeks, by application date.
command.allClear: Nothing is waiting on you right now.

jobWizard.step1Lead: Start with the title in Arabic and English. It's saved as a draft right away, and the next steps follow.
jobWizard.savedAsDraft: Saved as a draft. Nothing is published yet.
jobWizard.lead: Create, publish and follow every job. A new job opens a guided setup.
jobWizard.firstJobBody: Create your first job: a short guided sequence covers everything candidates need.

stepLead.details: Describe the role: what it involves, where, and for whom. Save this step, then continue.
stepLead.requirements: Add what a candidate needs: experience, education, certificates. Save each change, then continue.
stepLead.reference-skills: Confirm the skills this job needs. Save, then continue.
stepLead.assessment: Prepare the practical task candidates will complete. You can come back to it before publishing.
stepLead.review: Check that everything is ready, then publish.

missing.details: Add a description so candidates understand the role.
missing.requirements: No requirements yet. Recommended, not required.
missing.reference-skills: No skills yet. Skills connect the job to matching candidates.
missing.assessment: No assessment yet. Candidates can still apply.

jobWizard.publishBody: Publishing makes the job visible to candidates. You can unpublish or close it at any time.
jobWizard.descriptionHint: What the role does day to day and its main responsibilities, one per line. Fill in at least one language. MIDAN builds the requirements, the AI assessment draft and the requirements match from it.

orgAssessments.lead: Submissions waiting for your review, and how each job's assessments are progressing.
orgAssessments.toReviewLead: Proposed scores are only a starting point. A person on your team decides.
orgAssessments.progressLead: Where candidates are in each job's assessment.
orgAssessments.noAttemptsBody: Candidates receive the assessment once a job's assessment is published and they apply.

orgInterviews.lead: Every interview across your jobs, by day.
orgInterviews.ruleNote: An interview can only be scheduled for a shortlisted candidate. Schedule it from the candidate's page.
orgInterviews.readyToSchedule: {count} shortlisted candidates are ready for an interview.
orgInterviews.noUpcomingBody: Shortlist a candidate first, then schedule from their page.
orgInterviews.scheduleLead: Open a candidate to schedule their interview.
orgInterviews.howToStart: Interviews appear here once you shortlist candidates and schedule them.
orgInterviews.noneReady: No one is shortlisted yet. Shortlist a candidate to arrange an interview.

hiringBoard.lead: Every applicant in the stage they're in now. Change a status from the card; only the moves the system allows are offered.
hiringBoard.ruleInterview: Interviews need a shortlisted candidate first.
hiringBoard.ruleHire: You can mark a candidate as hired once they're evaluated or shortlisted; a shortlist isn't required. Every assessment must be reviewed first.

orgReports.lead: Your recruitment, from your organization's own records.
orgReports.emptyBody: Reports appear once you have jobs and applicants.
orgReports.volumeLead: Applications per week over the last twelve weeks.
orgReports.progressionLead: Where applicants are now, by stage. This shows positions, not rates between stages.
orgReports.jobsLead: Each job's applicants and assessment activity.
orgReports.limits: Not shown on purpose: time to hire and conversion rates between stages need each application's full history, which isn't available here yet. Scores aren't averaged across assessment versions because their criteria differ.

career.title: Where you're heading, and what's next
career.lead: Choose a professional destination, see what it asks for, and build evidence for it one step at a time. Everything here comes from your own records, and it stays yours whatever happens with any application.
career.loadFailed: Your career information couldn't be loaded just now. Refresh the page to try again.
career.source: Roles and skills come from the sector skills databases issued by the sectoral skills councils. Job families aren't official job titles.

destination.noneLead: Choose a role to see the skills it asks for and the next step toward it.
destination.family: {family}, in the {sector} sector, as the sector skills database describes it.
destination.titleOnly: A title in your own words. Link it to a job family to see the skills the sector database lists for it.

start.title: Start by choosing where you're heading
start.body: Pick a job family from the sector skills databases, or type a title in your own words. You'll see the skills the role asks for, and which of them nothing shows yet.

showcase.title: What MIDAN does today, honestly
showcase.lead: A recruitment and career-development platform where skills are shown through real work. This page separates what works and was tested from what runs on real services and what isn't built yet.

works.title: Implemented and tested
works.lead: Each item runs end to end on the local platform with fictional data, and is covered by automated tests.

items.title: Apply once, assess right away
items.body: Candidates apply to published jobs; duplicate applications open the existing one; the job's approved assessment is assigned on applying.
items.evidence: API end-to-end and browser journey tests

items.title: Job-specific assessments, published by people
items.body: Drafts are generated from the job's requirements, checked against the MIDAN Assessment Standard, edited and approved by the organization. Nothing is published automatically.
items.evidence: API end-to-end tests; the quality gate refuses drafts that aren't ready

items.title: Evaluation with human review
items.body: Written work is scored per criterion with a quote from the answer as evidence; every result waits for a person before it is released.

items.title: Requirements match with evidence
items.body: For each requirement: shown, partly shown, not shown or needs review, with the line from the submitted profile and a reason. Staff confirm or correct; nothing is decided automatically.
items.evidence: AI service and API end-to-end tests, including tenant isolation

items.title: Career journey
items.body: Choose a role from the sector skills databases, see its skills by evidence, plan learning, practise, and see L0–L4 levels. No readiness percentages.
items.evidence: Checked in the browser against the real API

items.title: Assistant grounded in your own records
items.body: Candidates and organizations ask questions; answers cite the records they used and link to the page where you act. It never acts itself.
items.evidence: AI service tests and API end-to-end permission tests

items.title: Interviews and hiring
items.body: Interviews only for shortlisted applicants, private video rooms, structured feedback, and decisions issued by people.

items.title: Organizations kept apart
items.body: Each organization sees only its own jobs, applicants and branding. Row-level security on every table.
items.evidence: Database security tests and cross-organization API tests

items.title: Arabic and English, light and dark
items.body: Right-to-left and left-to-right from the same screens, on phone, tablet and desktop.
items.evidence: Browser tests in both languages and both themes

real.title: Verified against the live providers
real.lead: These were exercised against the real services with fictional data, not mocks.

items.title: CV reading and scoring
items.body: Groq with openai/gpt-oss-120b reads CVs (personal details stay on MIDAN), drafts assessments and scores written work.
items.evidence: Real calls on 8 November 2026; the account's per-minute limit caps how many drafts run back to back

items.title: Video interviews
items.body: Private Daily.co rooms with a short-lived token per participant; everyone else is refused.
items.evidence: Real rooms created, joined and deleted on 8 November 2026

items.title: Calendar events
items.body: Interview events are created, moved and cancelled in Google Calendar, with attendee emails switched off in the demo.

planned.title: What isn't there, said plainly
planned.lead: These need a decision, a credential or more work. The platform doesn't pretend to do them.

items.title: Semantic matching models in production
items.body: multilingual-e5-base was measured locally; BAAI/bge-m3 needs a Hugging Face token to measure. Matching runs on word comparison until a model is chosen and deployed.

items.title: Email notifications
items.body: Notifications are in-app; no email provider is set up.

items.title: Saved jobs, report export, role responsibilities
items.body: Listed with proposed contracts in the frontend–backend handoff.

items.title: Production hosting
items.body: Everything shown runs on a local stack. Deployment, backups and monitoring follow the deployment and recovery checklists.

path.title: One hiring journey, end to end
path.note: The demo uses synthetic organizations, jobs and people, all labelled as such, on a local copy of the platform.

steps.title: Publish a job
steps.body: Requirements, skills and an approved, job-specific assessment.

steps.title: Apply and do the work
steps.body: A real scenario with a deadline, saved as it goes.

steps.title: Review with evidence
steps.body: Scores with quotes, the requirements match, and a person's review.

steps.title: Interview and decide
steps.body: A private room, feedback, and a decision issued by people.

showcase.honesty: MIDAN is under development. Nothing on this page refers to customers, revenue or prices; the examples are fictional.
showcase.closing: See it with real work, not promises
